neighbours.label: a verb for a life-course ending or turning point, mainly dying ('died', 'die', 'passed away'), also resigning or starting treatment
fire: The female lays her eggs in late summer and the adults die soon afterwards.
His grandfather emigrated in 1920 and died in Chicago thirty years later.
The composer fell ill on tour and died before finishing the symphony.
Her husband passed away in the spring, and she sold the farm that autumn.
The general resigned his command after the defeat at the river.
Many of the soldiers died of fever before they reached the coast.
The poet's mother died when he was nine, and he was raised by an aunt.
Most of the seedlings die within a week if the soil dries out.
quiet: The female lays her eggs in late summer and the adults stay near the nest.
His grandfather emigrated in 1920 and opened a bakery in Chicago.
The composer fell ill on tour and rested for a month in Vienna.
Her husband grew wheat in the spring, and she sold the eggs that autumn.
The general praised his officers after the victory at the river.
Many of the soldiers sang songs at night before they reached the coast.
The poet's mother was a teacher, and he grew up in a house full of books.
Most of the seedlings grow quickly if the soil stays moist.

notes: Card: ' died' lift 1,998 among the top tokens, with peaks on events before a time phrase. Probe: 'die a few weeks later' 0.44, 'passed away / died two years later' 0.37, 'began chemotherapy' 0.31 with or without a time phrase, 'resigned his seat' 0.27; matched non-event versions 0.03-0.10. So the time adjunct is not needed; the event verb drives it. Quiet items keep the biographical narratives without a death or ending.
